description: For business tools companies keep records in (chat, email, tickets, docs, CRM, call recordings, code hosts): who owns the customer's data, whether the vendor trains AI on it (generative and other models, by plan), whether it keeps aggregated use, what can be exported on which plan and by whom, how much history the plan keeps, and how long data stays after cancellation. Each answer is quoted word for word from the vendor's own terms, AI page, data processing addendum or help article, with the date read. "The terms don't say" means every contract was read and none answers; "Not read yet" means a document is still unread. Answers marked inferred are a reading of the text, not its words. Not legal advice.

answer.description: Keep tools whose headline answer has this token, e.g. opt_out with field=ai_training.

facts.description: false = headline answers only, no quoted facts. Default true.

field.description: One question: ownership, ai_training, aggregate_use, export, retention or after_cancel.

plan.description: A plan name as the vendor spells it, e.g. "Free", "Enterprise".

record_type.description: Kind of record: slack-and-teams, email, support-tickets, jira-and-linear, crm, call-recordings, documents-and-sops.

tool.description: Tool id, e.g. "slack", "microsoft-365", "google-workspace", "salesforce", "notion". Omit to list every tool.

name: get_tool_terms
title: What a business tool's terms say about customer data
